deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft for Riemann's 1861 memoir 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines flüssigen gleichartigen Ellipsoides'. The previous page sets up the 'second case': rotation about one axis only (u=u'=v=v'=0). In that case the conserved quantities give (a-b)^2 w = (v+v1)/2 and (a+b)^2 w' = (v-v1)/2, which the page calls τ, τ'. For steady figures (a,b,c constant) the governing function is the one written at the head of this page (and on the previous page):
  G(a,b,c) = τ²/(a-b)² + τ'²/(a+b)² - κ,  with κ = 2επ·abc·∫_0^∞ ds/Δ, Δ = sqrt((a²+s)(b²+s)(c²+s)), and the constraint abc = a0 b0 c0.
Equilibrium figures are the stationary points of G under the volume constraint. Riemann's stability criterion is that G be a minimum.

The page is mostly upside down and badly smudged. It can be read with reasonable confidence as Riemann computing the second variation of G at an equilibrium. Several of the transcribed lines read 'r', '(a-b)²/r²' and similar; in the image these are evidently τ²/(a-b)², τ'²/(a+b)², and so on.

(1) First variation. Riemann works with logarithmic derivatives. Because τ²/(a-b)² and τ'²/(a+b)² are homogeneous of degree -2 in (a,b), we have (a∂_a + b∂_b) applied to them equal to -2 times them. Combinations such as 2τ²/(a-b)² + 2τ'²/(a+b)² and 4τ²/(a-b)², 4τ'²/(a+b)² are therefore expressed through derivatives of κ in suitable variables. In the lines '4(a-b)²/r² = ...' and '4(a+b)²/r'² = ...' the left sides are presumably 4τ²/(a-b)² and 4τ'²/(a+b)².
- One of the combinations is (b-a)/... + (b+a)/... = 2b/(b²-a²).
- From the stationarity conditions one gets the relation τ²/(b-a)³ = τ'²/(b+a)³. This appears on the previous page in the special case a = c.

(2) Second variation. The τ-terms contribute
  d²[τ²/(a-b)²] = 6τ²(δa-δb)²/(a-b)⁴,
  d²[τ'²/(a+b)²] = 6τ'²(δa+δb)²/(a+b)⁴.
Riemann writes these as the lines 'δ²q = 6 (a-b)⁴... (δa-δb)² + (a+b)⁴...(δa+δb)²', with the τ's misread. To these he adds -δ²κ.

(3) Change of variables. To handle δ²κ, he introduces logarithmic coordinates x, p, q. The equations δx = δq - δp, dx = 2q dp and similar are garbled and uncertain. He also introduces quadratic quantities, with a reading of α = (a²+b²)/2, β = (a²-b²)/2 (uncertain). He records their log-derivatives:
  ∂logα/∂x = β+γ,  ∂logα/∂p = β-γ,  ∂logα/∂q = -2γ,
  ∂logβ/∂x = α+γ,  ∂logβ/∂p = α-γ,
  log α = 2p + const,  log β = q - p + const,  log γ = -q - p + const.
Here γ is presumably a third such quantity involving c. This is the same device as on the next page, which uses ρ = (a²+c²)/(2b²) and α = (a²-c²)/(2b²), with ∂ρ/∂log b = -2ρ and so on.

In these variables he obtains linear relations such as δx = 2(α dq - 3β dp) and δq = 2(β dq - 3α dp) (my reading, uncertain). He then gets a quadratic form for δ²q of the shape 4(α dq² - 6β dp dq + 9α dp²). Using equilibrium relations of the type 'κ = (1/ι) q' (garbled), he assembles the full second variation as a quadratic form in δp, δq. Its coefficients are combinations like (∂q/∂x - ∂p/∂x + 4q), (a² - 4ι²)(∂q/∂x - 2q) and 4(b²-a²)(∂q/∂x - q). The sign of this form decides whether G has a minimum.

The detailed coefficient bookkeeping cannot be reliably reconstructed from the image. Beyond the structure described, I mark it as unreadable rather than guessing.

Purpose: the stability (minimum of G) of the one-axis-rotation equilibria. These comprise the Maclaurin, Jacobi and Dedekind figures and the Riemann S-type ellipsoids. This material appears in condensed form in §§ of the 1861 paper.
errors: Many intermediate lines are crossed out and rewritten; several of Riemann's own coefficient computations visibly change (e.g. '-4' struck to '2' in the δp δq term), indicating trial-and-error bookkeeping rather than a finished derivation.
The verifiable pieces (second differential of τ²/(a-b)² being 6τ²(δa-δb)²/(a-b)⁴; homogeneity relations) are correct.
The full quadratic-form coefficients are too illegible to check.

Historically, Riemann's energy-minimum criterion is sufficient but was treated by him as if it delimited stability. Lebovitz (1966) and Chandrasekhar showed that his stability conclusions for S-type ellipsoids are incomplete. That is an issue of the method, not an algebraic slip on this page.

results.what: Equilibrium of one-axis-rotating fluid ellipsoids as stationary points of G = τ²/(a-b)² + τ'²/(a+b)² - 2επ abc∫ds/Δ under abc = const
results.modern_name: Riemann ellipsoids (S-type) / energy (Lagrangian) function for self-gravitating ellipsoids

results.what: Second variation of G in logarithmic/quadratic coordinates to test whether G is a minimum (stability)
results.modern_name: Riemann's stability criterion for Riemann ellipsoids (energy minimum), later refined by Lebovitz–Lifschitz

results.what: Closed form ∫_0^∞ ds/((s+ρ)√(s+1)) = (1/√(1-ρ)) log((1+√(1-ρ))/(1-√(1-ρ))) used for the potential in the spheroidal case (previous/next page)

deep.surprise_reason: These are working drafts of the stability computation for the 1861 Riemann-ellipsoid paper. The content (energy function, second variation, change to logarithmic variables) is known to be Riemann's and published in condensed form. Nothing here goes beyond it.

transcription_corrections: Most of the page is written upside down; the transcription's 'r', 'r'' should be τ, τ', and the fractions are inverted: '(a-b)²/r²' is τ²/(a-b)², and '(a+b)²/r'²' is τ'²/(a+b)².
The heading line should read τ²/(a-b)² + τ'²/(a+b)² - κ (the function G of the previous page), not (a-b)²/r² + ...
'δ²q = 6(a-b)⁴/r²(δa-δb)² + ...' is better read as δ²G containing 6τ²/(a-b)⁴ (δa-δb)² + 6τ'²/(a+b)⁴ (δa+δb)².

Symbols transcribed as 'ι' and 'x' are uncertain; 'ι' may be a letter for a constant (possibly ε or c²), and several 'log α' / 'log β' lines likely refer to quadratic quantities in a², b², c² analogous to ρ, α on the next page.
